title: IAU definition of planet - Wikipedia
snippet: In August 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) adopted a new definition of the term planet, which stated that, in the Solar System, [a] a planet is a celestial body that: is in orbit around the Sun, has sufficient mass to assume hydrostatic equilibrium (a nearly round shape), and has "cleared the neighbourhood" around its orbit.

snippet: 2006: IAU Resolution B5 (Definition of a Planet in the Solar System) explicitly lists the eight planets Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

title: The Classification and Count of Planets in Our Solar System
snippet: Jun 6, 2026 · In modern astronomy, the definition of a planet is dictated by the International Astronomical Union (IAU). As of June 6, 2026, there are eight officially recognized planets in our solar system. This count was established in 2006 following the reclassification of Pluto, a decision that sparked significant scientific and public debate.
